title: Freshwater ops handoff - weekly snapshot
content:
Quick summary

This is the weekly SRE handoff note for the Freshwater cluster (us-west-2, GPU pool #3). Focus this week: incident on 2029-08-06 that produced a sustained 99p latency breach, SLO status and mitigations, planned follow-ups, and the on-call handoff log. Document is intentionally rough — capturing timelines and action owners for the postmortem draft.

Attendees / on-call
- On-call (primary): Jonah Kim
- On-call (secondary): Priya Singh
- Incident lead (infra): Liam O'Connor
- Runtime engineer: Sara Müller
- Notes owner / coordinator: Maya Patel

High-level incident narrative (2029-08-06)
- 09:02 PDT: Observability alert triggered — Freshwater GPU pool 3 99th-percentile request latency > 400ms for the hosted text-generation API route (/v1/generate/redwood-slim).
- 09:03: Automated paging to on-call primary. Large increase in queued RPCs and GPU worker load observed.
- 09:05: Canary autoscaler started scale-up to 8 extra pods, but pods failed healthchecks and fell into CrashLoop between 09:06-09:12.
- 09:10: Traffic was routed to Dedicated fallback pool per routing policy (region-failover). Tail latency remained elevated (99p ~ 420ms) due to cold-starts and degraded batching efficiency.
- 09:18: Incident lead identified elevated GPU OOM patterns in runtime logs; several workers flagged high GPU memory use from a leak in the kv-cache retention path when sequence-length > 2k.
- 09:25: Emergency mitigation — disabled automatic prefix caching for the affected model variant and reduced max_batch_size to force smaller in-flight batches.
- 09:42: Latency returned under SLO (99p < 200ms) for user-facing traffic; mitigation kept in place while rollback candidate was prepared.
- 10:30: Incident declared resolved for customer-impacting symptoms; continued monitoring and follow-up tasks created.

Immediate impact and customer scope
- Duration: ~40 minutes of SLO breach; customer-visible slow responses for ~20 minutes before failover kicked in.
- Affected routes: hosted text generation for the redwood-slim model family in us-west-2 (estimated 0.8% of total traffic at peak).
- No data loss, no authentication failures reported.

SLO snapshot (weekly)
- Latency SLO (hosted generate, regional): 99p <= 200ms.
- This week (7-day rolling): 99p = 182ms (within SLO) except the 2029-08-06 spike that produced a transient breach.
- Error budget: pre-incident remaining budget: 84% for the monthly cycle. After the incident, budget dipped to 79% (still within budget but flagged for review).

Root cause hypothesis (preliminary)
1) Runtime regression in kv-cache retention introduced in runtime PR #1284 — under certain long-sequence workloads (>2k tokens) the cache retention logic failed to free ephemeral buffers, causing gradual GPU memory growth.
2) Autoscaler healthcheck timing and startup probe were too aggressive for the model variant's cold-start characteristics; new pods failed healthchecks before KV cache initialization completed.
3) Workflow-level mixing of large and small sequences increased batching variance, reducing batching efficiency during failover and exacerbating tail latency.

Mitigations applied during incident
- Disabled prefix/KV caching for the affected variant (config toggle roll back) to prevent additional leaks while investigating.
- Reduced max_batch_size from 16 -> 6 for the variant in Freshwater pool to bound per-pod memory pressure.
- Rerouted ~65% of incoming traffic to regional fallback pool while fixes were staged.

Post-incident follow-ups / action items (owners & tickets)
- SRE-4821: Full postmortem writeup + incident timeline (owner: Jonah Kim).
- RTE-1296: Revert/patch runtime PR #1284 with safe cache free path and add memory-use unit tests (owner: Sara Müller, linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287).
- INFRA-2302: Adjust autoscaler startup probe and healthcheck grace period for GPU workers with heavy model init (owner: Liam O'Connor).
- SRE-4824: Create workload classification rule to split long-sequence traffic to a dedicated node-pool (owner: Priya Singh).
- OBS-900: Add a synthetic long-sequence producer in canary to exercise kv-cache paths in pre-release tests (owner: Maya Patel).

Planned timeline for follow-ups
- 2029-08-09: RTE patch landed to staging; memory regression tests added.
- 2029-08-11: Autoscaler probe adjustment rolled to staging.
- 2029-08-14: Canary long-sequence synthetic test run and monitoring evaluation.
- 2029-08-16: If green, roll fixes to Freshwater pool; monitor 72h.

Monitoring / dashboards updated
- Added a temporary SLO revision dashboard showing 1h/6h/24h 99p latency and GPU mem-resident-per-process for Freshwater pool.
- Synthetic job created to exercise long-sequence path every 15 minutes in staging.

Notes for the on-call who’s taking over
- Current active mitigations: prefix/KV caching disabled for redwood-slim variant in Freshwater pool; max_batch_size = 6 set for that variant.
- Watch key metrics (alerts already configured): gpu_mem_usage_per_process > 85% (warning), 99p_latency_hosted_generate_us-west-2 > 250ms (page), worker_restart_rate > 1/min (warn).
- If tail latency deviates again: first step is to force-evict warm KV caches across pool and keep traffic steer to fallback pool while we evaluate. Evictions safe via config rollback playbook: Confluence link in linked_artifacts.
- Slack incident channel: #ops-incident-freshwater (link in linked_artifacts). Use incident template SRE-INC-TEMPLATE when paging to execs.

Retro notes / learnings (informal)
- Mixing workload classes on the same node-pool (short conversational prompts + long analytical sequences) created unpredictable batching shapes. We should favor static classification and routing for known long-sequence workflows.
- Autoscaler and healthchecks need a more gradual warm-up path for heavy model variants — consider a two-phase health check (binary readiness after init, then warm-readiness tied to kv-cache priming).
- Observability blindspot: we didn’t have a synthetic long-sequence canary in production causing delayed detection of regression. The short-term synthetic will help, but long-term we need to add this to the release gating checklist.

Final items before handoff
- Jonah: finalize incident timeline and assign SRE-4821.
- Sara: push runtime patch to staging and tag RTE-1296.
- Liam: land autoscaler probe change in staging and schedule greenlight.
- Priya: prototype request-routing rule in test cluster and document cost implications.

Next on-call rotation
- Primary (starting 2029-08-10 08:00 PDT): Priya Singh
- Secondary: Liam O'Connor

If you pick this up after hours: prioritize stabilizing user-facing latency — use traffic-steering and batch-reduction toggles in the operations console. If unable to contain within 30 minutes escalate to infra PM and runtime lead per the incident escalation policy.

End of handoff note.
